scenes.line1: How does .NET run your code fast?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how .NET makes your code run so fast? Let's break down CLR, JIT, tiered compilation, and AOT.

scenes.label: CLR
scenes.sub: Executes managed code and handles memory.
scenes.say: First up, the Common Language Runtime, or CLR, runs your managed code and takes care of memory and execution.

rows.b: Converts IL to native at runtime
Quick compile, then optimize hot code

scenes.say: The Just-In-Time compiler, or JIT, turns intermediate language into native code as needed. Tiered compilation speeds up startup by compiling fast, then optimizing methods that run a lot.
Ahead-Of-Time, or AOT, compiles to native code before you run the app. JIT adapts at runtime but starts slower. AOT gives you faster startup.

scenes.question: Is AOT always better than JIT?
scenes.right: No. JIT allows runtime optimizations; AOT is faster to start but less adaptive.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Is AOT always better than JIT? No way. JIT can optimize as your app runs, while AOT is all about fast startup.
